values: Scope: submit-triggered behavior only for Initial Form, HTML/REST Progressive Form, and Schedule Appointment Form. Includes positive, negative, partial-success, duplicate, and risk cases; excludes pre-submit rendering, validation, prefill, filtering, and calendar display.

QA setup: replace placeholder contacts/opportunities/users/calendars with disposable test records. Record actual IDs and environment details in Notes or Evidence Link. Verify both intended effects and stated non-effects after every submission.
GHL connection, pipeline, default routing, state-to-user mapping, user-to-stage mapping, redirect URL, and relevant custom fields are configured.
Valid email and phone; state with an assigned user; first/last name, role, interest, event address/date, company, and message populated.
Submission succeeds and redirects with contact_id and opportunity_id query parameters.
Contact is upserted; assignedTo matches the state-routed user; tags contain lead and '<assigned user first name> lead'; standard fields and resolvable contact custom fields are saved.
A new open opportunity is created in the configured pipeline and routed stage, assigned to the same user, with source Website Form, value 0, and resolvable opportunity custom fields.
Plugin logs successful contact and opportunity creation and adds the redirect URL to the Elementor response.
No appointment is created; no progressive webhook is sent; strong lead and scheduled tags are not added.
Successful submission uses default routing when state mapping is unavailable
Default user and default pipeline stage are configured; submitted state is unmapped or blank.
Valid contact details with an unmapped state.
Submission succeeds and redirects with both generated IDs.
Contact is upserted and assigned to the configured default user; lead and user-specific lead tags are applied when that user's first name is available.
Opportunity is created in the default stage and assigned to the default user.
Fallback routing is logged for audit.
No state-mapped user or stage is used.
GHL is fully configured. Execute once for each supported role value.
Role is Event Professional, Wedding Venue Representative, or Hotel Representative; valid contact details.
Submit the Initial Form for each listed role.
Each successful submission redirects to https://gotoshoutdashboard.godesqsites.com with contact_id and opportunity_id.
Contact and its role custom field are saved normally.
The role-specific dashboard URL overrides the configured form/dashboard redirect.
The configured non-dashboard redirect is not used for these roles.
Role comparison is case-insensitive after trimming.

Submission redirects to the configured URL with contact_id and opportunity_id.

No rollback removes the contact or possible opportunity.

Valid payload includes role, interest, event address, and event date.
Submission still succeeds if the main contact and opportunity calls succeed.

Base opportunity and any resolvable custom fields are saved; unresolved fields are omitted.

Routing resolves a user ID, but saved GHL user metadata has no usable first name/name.

A successful Initial Form submission already exists for the same email/phone.
Submit the same Initial Form payload again.
Second submission is processed as a new request and returns its own successful response if GHL accepts it.

The plugin calls create opportunity again; verify that an additional opportunity is created and record its ID.
The plugin performs no idempotency check and does not suppress the repeat opportunity creation.
Expected contact deduplication ultimately depends on GHL upsert behavior.
Valid QA contact/opportunity IDs; GHL configured; relevant opportunity custom fields exist.
Populate one or more text/select fields across the allowed event sections; no file upload.
POST the HTML form once to /wp-json/ghl-elementor/v1/progressive-form/opportunity.
HTTP success with success=true, 'Event details were submitted.', and the mapped updated_fields list.

Success response lists every mapped custom-field key that was updated.
Strong lead is added and lead is removed.
Each non-empty form field lands in its corresponding opportunity custom field; empty fields are omitted.
Webhook payload contains IDs, venue size, product type/floor, and the configured detail/notes fields.
No blank custom-field values overwrite fields that were not submitted.
Successful standard fields plus inspiration file upload

Valid IDs and otherwise mapped form field names.
HTTP success says no event details were submitted; updated_fields=[].
No invalid custom-field IDs are written.
A successful standard Progressive Form submission has completed.
Reuse the same IDs and identical standard field values.

The same opportunity fields are written again.
No idempotency key or duplicate suppression prevents repeated side effects.
A successful file submission has completed.
Reuse the same IDs and upload the same local file again.
File field is cleared and set again to a new unique upload URL.
A second WordPress file is stored and webhook is sent again.
Previous WordPress upload is not deleted and duplicate suppression is not applied.
Multiple files supplied to one inspiration field
Valid IDs; client or direct API test permits multiple files for one field.
Attach two valid files under the same field key.
Tag operations run after the opportunity update.
Only the first uploaded URL is placed in the GHL custom field.
All accepted files may be stored in WordPress; webhook is sent.
Extra uploaded files are not referenced in GHL and are not removed.
GHL configured; QA contact has assigned user; that user has a configured calendar.
